title: Edward Clem, James McNeil and Wendell, and bands changing personnel
summary: Clem was a so-so cornetist who may not have read music; McNeil was a teacher and bandleader; his brother Wendell played with everyone as bands broke up quickly.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Edward Clem? He's a nice cornet player, trumpet player. In those days they called it cornet. Didn't say trumpet like they do now. Edward Clem, he's pretty good.
Was he blonde or could he see a little or could he see well?

Well, he could see pretty good. I knew he would have blue eyeglasses all the time. He lived over there on Erata Street there. On Erata and Howard for years. Edward Clem. He had a, he was just a so-so record. He wasn't such a very big folly. He didn't draw much water, he didn't.
Now could he read music was what I was getting at?
Not that I knew of. Not that I knew of. I don't think Edward was a musician. James McNeill was a master musician.
James was a teacher and more of a band leader. And more of an instructor and a band leader. And it all comes to playing on the trumpet.
What about his brother? You know his brother? Played fiddle, Wendell?

Oh, Wendell played with all of them. He played with all, at different times with all of them. Wendell did. See these fellas, getting out his daddy. In those days, all of them played around with each other. See? Even though you have a band tonight. Now this is your band tonight. Now next week you're in somebody else's band. See, because bands broke up just that fast. The bosses let you out just that fast. They didn't have to notify you. He let you out. They let you out. They wouldn't let you out. They split the band up. They wouldn't play anybody. He would play with you. You'd play with you. You'd play with you. You'd play with you. You'd play with you. That's why I was playing around so much.
